articles.headline: Derribo del tapón de Doña Urraca: Lugo elimina un punto negro y abre un nuevo ciclo de obras
articles.subtitle: La casa que bloquea el cruce de Doña Urraca con Camiño Verde y Mar Cantábrico empieza a demolerse este jueves tras retirarse el fibrocemento. El derribo permitirá completar la Segunda Ronda y da paso a nuevas obras en la ciudad.
articles.body:
El Concello de Lugo arranca este jueves la demolición de la casa que tapona el cruce de las calles Doña Urraca, Camiño Verde y Mar Cantábrico, en A Piringalla. Durante el miércoles se retiró el fibrocemento del inmueble, una actuación previa necesaria por la presencia de amianto. El edificio, contra el que impactó un vehículo en 2023, es uno de los tapones urbanísticos más conocidos de la ciudad.

La demolición eliminará un punto de inseguridad y de feísmo en el barrio y permitirá completar la Segunda Ronda. Las obras están cofinanciadas por el plan Novo Norte, que moviliza 8,7 millones de fondos europeos y 5,8 millones propios antes del 31 de diciembre de 2030.

El gobierno local mantiene otros frentes abiertos: la pasarela sobre la avenida República Argentina, entre los parques Rosalía de Castro y Marcos Cela, se adjudicará en las próximas semanas tras las dudas de Adega; la Xunta construye un parque canino de más de 3.750 metros cuadrados en Fontiñas y aportará 225.000 euros, la mitad del coste, para un aparcamiento disuasorio en O Ceao. Siguen pendientes la expropiación de un edificio en Camiño de Pipín y la acera ante el colegio de As Gándaras.

La Asociación de Vecinos de A Milagrosa llevaba años reclamando la intervención por el riesgo del inmueble, en ruinas desde hace tiempo. El Concello confía en que el derribo, ejecutado con maquinaria, se complete a lo largo de la jornada.

articles.headline: La rebaja de 20 céntimos del gasóleo ahorrará 5,5 millones al mes a los conductores lucenses
articles.subtitle: El Gobierno activa en septiembre la cláusula de salvaguarda tras el repunte del 15,7% del gasóleo en julio. Según el IGE, en Lugo se consumieron 328,7 millones de litros en 2025, lo que supondrá un ahorro de unos 66 millones al año.
articles.body:
La rebaja fiscal de 20 céntimos por litro en el Impuesto sobre Hidrocarburos volverá a aplicarse al gasóleo en septiembre, después de que el IPC de julio confirmara una subida interanual del 15,7%, por encima del umbral del 15% que activa la cláusula de salvaguarda del plan de respuesta a la guerra en Irán. La gasolina, que subió un 7,3%, mantendrá una rebaja de solo 5 céntimos.

El impacto en Lugo será notable. Según los datos del Instituto Galego de Estadística citados por El Progreso, en la provincia se consumieron 279.464 toneladas de gasóleo A y B en 2025, unos 328,7 millones de litros. Con la rebaja de septiembre, los conductores lucenses ahorrarán alrededor de 5,5 millones de euros al mes y cerca de 66 millones al año, siempre que los precios se mantengan.

El gasóleo A, el de uso general en los vehículos, supone el 77,3% del consumo provincial, mientras que el B, destinado a maquinaria agrícola e industrial, representa el 22,7%. La rebaja equivale a unos diez euros por cada depósito de 50 litros y no afecta al gasóleo C de calefacción. El precio del gasóleo subió un 14,5% en Galicia en el último año.

El presidente de Tradime, José Fernández, pidió agilidad en la aplicación de la medida para que el descuento llegue cuanto antes al surtidor. El Ministerio de Economía calcula un coste fiscal de 1.825 millones para el conjunto del Estado.

articles.headline: La quema de ruedas en O Carqueixo obliga a un gran despliegue para sofocar un incendio de 12 hectáreas
articles.subtitle: Una columna de humo negro, visible desde casi toda la ciudad, alertó en la tarde del miércoles del fuego declarado junto al poblado de O Carqueixo, en la parroquia de Bóveda. El incendio quedó controlado sobre las siete de la tarde.
articles.body:
Una enorme columna de humo negro se hizo visible este miércoles desde casi cualquier punto de Lugo. El origen estaba en las inmediaciones del poblado de O Carqueixo, en la parroquia de Bóveda, donde unas personas sin identificar prendieron fuego a un montón de ruedas y residuos con el objetivo de extraer los metales con los que se fabrican.

El fuego, declarado en un día de riesgo extremo de incendio, calcinó unas 12 hectáreas y obligó a un gran despliegue de medios: un helicóptero y dos avionetas de la Xunta, cuatro brigadas y cuatro camiones, además de seis bomberos y dos motobombas del Concello de Lugo.

Las llamas quedaron controladas sobre las 19.00 horas, aunque los efectivos mantuvieron retenes durante la noche para vigilar posibles reactivaciones. La gran humareda, visible a varios kilómetros, generó numerosas llamadas al 112 y un aluvión de avisos en las redes sociales.

No es la primera vez que se registran incendios de este tipo en la zona, donde el material abandonado se convierte en un riesgo recurrente en verano.

articles.headline: La apertura completa de la A-54 acumula ocho meses de retraso y sigue sin fecha
articles.subtitle: El último tramo por abrir, los 16 kilómetros entre Melide y Arzúa, debería estar acabado desde enero, pero las obras se han ralentizado en el enlace con la villa arzuana. El Gobierno insiste en que la puesta en servicio será lo antes posible.
articles.body:
La apertura completa de la autovía A-54, que une Lugo con Santiago, sigue sin fecha. El último tramo por abrir, los 16 kilómetros entre Melide y Arzúa, debería haberse concluido en enero, pero acumula ocho meses de retraso y el Ministerio de Transportes se limita a repetir que la puesta en servicio se producirá lo antes posible.

El principal punto de fricción es el enlace con Arzúa, donde los trabajos se han ralentizado. El Concello arzuano lleva meses exigiendo una reunión urgente con el Ministerio, mientras el BNG local reclama que la vía no se abra sin las garantías de seguridad necesarias. El Ministerio atribuyó parte del retraso a mejoras añadidas a las obras y a los episodios de tormentas.

La A-54 ha ido abriéndose por tramos desde 2025: el de Palas de Rei-Melide entró en servicio el 3 de febrero de ese año. Cuando se complete el tramo final, la autovía unirá por completo las dos capitales gallegas y permitirá circular de Lugo a Santiago sin recurrir a la AP-9 ni a las carreteras nacionales.

articles.headline: El Gobierno trasladará a unas 500 menores vulnerables de Ceuta a la Península y Feijóo anuncia batalla judicial
articles.subtitle: El plan de acogida, coordinado por el secretario de Estado Rubén Pérez, prioriza a niñas y perfiles más vulnerables con la acogida de todas las comunidades. Feijóo exige devolver a Marruecos en un mes a todos los migrantes y llevará el plante del Gobierno al Supremo.
articles.body:
El Ministerio de Juventud e Infancia trabaja en un plan para trasladar de manera urgente a la Península a unas 500 menores migrantes no acompañadas que se encuentran en Ceuta tras la entrada masiva del 30 de julio. El secretario de Estado Rubén Pérez coordina desde el domingo un plan integral que combina la acogida vinculante y solidaria de las comunidades autónomas, el acogimiento familiar y la vía de organizaciones de protección a la infancia sin trasladar la tutela.

La ministra Sira Rego considera una barbaridad deportar a los menores y defiende un retorno voluntario con garantías, mientras Elma Saiz anunció 25 millones de euros de acompañamiento. La Policía Nacional ha identificado a 2.168 menores desde el 30 de julio.

En la oposición, Alberto Núñez Feijóo visita este miércoles Ceuta y exige la devolución de todos los que entraron ilegalmente, mayores y menores, como mucho en un mes. El líder del PP anunció que llevará al Tribunal Supremo el plante del Gobierno al Senado, donde los ministros no comparecen, y que su grupo reprobará a cinco ministros. La ciudad autónoma, con capacidad ordinaria para 29 plazas, soporta una presión superior al 4.600%.

Bruselas avala el retorno de los menores no acompañados siempre que se respete su interés superior, mientras el Gobierno insiste en que devolverlos a Marruecos sin garantías sería ilegal.

articles.headline: El incendio de Las Hurdes quema ya 3.700 hectáreas y obliga a desalojar doce núcleos
articles.subtitle: El fuego, declarado el martes en Pinofranqueado, es de tipo convectivo y generó dos pirocúmulos. Más de 700 vecinos permanecen fuera de sus casas y los equipos trabajan contra reloj con la humedad nocturna como aliada.
articles.body:
El incendio forestal de Las Hurdes, en Cáceres, ha calcinado ya unas 3.700 hectáreas, 2.100 de ellas en las últimas 24 horas, y obliga a mantener desalojados a más de 700 vecinos de doce núcleos de Pinofranqueado y Nuñomoral. La localidad de Asegur pudo volver a sus casas, mientras Nuñomoral permanece confinado.

El fuego, declarado el martes a las 14.30 en una cuneta de la CC-122 entre Robledo y Avellanar, presenta un perfil convectivo, es decir, genera su propia meteorología, y durante la tarde llegó a formar dos pirocúmulos. El alcalde de Pinofranqueado, José Luis Azabal, sostiene que el incendio fue intencionado: no hubo tormenta ni rayos y la hora de inicio no es habitual.

En la zona trabajan dos batallones de la UME, unos 170 efectivos del Infoex y 26 medios aéreos. La noche, con humedad cercana al 100% y viento en calma, abrió una gran ventana de oportunidad para los equipos de extinción. El fuego llegó a cruzar a Salamanca por el pico Las Tiendas, con focos ya controlados.

La presidenta extremeña, María Guardiola, fue increpada por evacuados durante su visita a la zona: El alcalde y la presidenta no hacen nada. Tres viviendas resultaron afectadas en Avellanar y 34 usuarios del centro Cottolengo fueron trasladados a Plasencia.

articles.headline: Moderna y Merck logran el primer ensayo en fase III positivo para una vacuna personalizada contra el melanoma
articles.subtitle: La terapia combina la vacuna de neoantígenos intismeran autogene con Keytruda y superó los objetivos en pacientes con melanoma en estadio IIB-IV. Es el primer resultado positivo en fase III para una terapia contra el cáncer basada en ARNm.
articles.body:
Moderna y Merck anunciaron este miércoles resultados positivos del ensayo de fase III INTerpath-001, que estudia la combinación de la vacuna personalizada de neoantígenos intismeran autogene con el fármaco Keytruda en más de 1.100 pacientes con melanoma en estadio IIB-IV al que se le había extirpado el tumor.

El ensayo cumplió su objetivo principal, prolongar la supervivencia libre de recaída, y el secundario, reducir el riesgo de metástasis a distancia, frente a Keytruda en monoterapia. Las compañías lo califican como el primer resultado positivo en fase III para una terapia de neoantígenos individualizada y para una terapia contra el cáncer basada en ARNm.

La investigadora principal, Georgina Long, directora médica del Melanoma Institute Australia, habla de un momento histórico para el tratamiento adyuvante del melanoma: es el primer estudio en demostrar que un tratamiento diseñado a partir de la huella mutacional de cada tumor reduce el riesgo de recaída o muerte.

En bolsa, Moderna llegó a subir más de un 130% en Wall Street, con picos intradía cercanos al 176%, mientras Merck avanzó alrededor de un 10%. La capitalización de Merck ronda los 333.000 millones de dólares y la de Moderna, los 25.000 millones.

articles.headline: La vuelta al cole más cara de la historia: 429 euros de media por alumno
articles.subtitle: El gasto medio por estudiante sube siete euros respecto al curso pasado y supera los 500 euros con calzado y material extra. Galicia figura entre las comunidades con mayores incrementos, aunque sus precios siguen por debajo de la media estatal.
articles.body:
La vuelta al cole de este curso será la más cara de la historia. Según el estudio de Banqmi-iAhorro recogido por RTVE, el gasto medio por alumno alcanzará los 429 euros, siete más que el año pasado, y superará los 505 euros si se suman calzado y material extra, según Idealo.

El desembolso varía mucho según el centro: unos 332 euros en la escuela pública, 446 en la concertada y 508 en la privada, según iAhorro. La Asociación Española de Consumidores eleva la horquilla hasta los 635 euros en centros públicos y 1.849 en privados con matrícula incluida. La Comunidad Valenciana es la más cara, con 487 euros, y Extremadura, la más barata.

Galicia figura entre las comunidades con mayores subidas, por encima del 2,5%, aunque el gasto medio en los centros públicos gallegos se sitúa en 566 euros, por debajo de la media estatal. La ropa y los uniformes suponen la mayor partida, con 234 euros de media, seguidos de los libros, unos 195.

La reutilización y la segunda mano permiten ahorrar hasta 200 euros por hijo. Además, sigue abierta hasta el 10 de septiembre la ayuda de 400 euros del Ministerio de Educación para alumnado con necesidad específica de apoyo educativo.

articles.headline: Mike Nesbitt resigns as health minister in row with UUP leader over Causeway Hospital
articles.subtitle: Nesbitt quit after learning via the media about Jon Burrows' second red line, this time against moving emergency general surgery from Causeway Hospital to Antrim. The UUP has seven days to nominate a replacement amid warnings of shockwaves across the health service.
articles.body:
Mike Nesbitt resigned as Northern Ireland's health minister on Wednesday, saying he discovered his party leader's position through the media rather than from him. The row centres on Jon Burrows' opposition to withdrawing emergency general surgery from Causeway Hospital and moving it to Antrim Area Hospital.

In his resignation letter, Nesbitt described the shockwaves the decision had created across the health and social care system and noted it was Burrows' second red line, after the Pathways service earlier in the year. The UUP now has seven days to nominate a replacement, with Robbie Butler reported to be the frontrunner.

Health bodies rallied behind the outgoing minister. Roisin Coulter, chair of the NI Confederation for Health and Social Care, said Nesbitt had listened to clinical leaders and urged that the momentum of the Reset Plan not stop. The BMA's Dr Alan Stout said Nesbitt put patient safety above politics, while Sinn Féin's Philip McGuigan said he believed Nesbitt had the interests of patients first.

Burrows thanked Nesbitt for taking on arguably the hardest job in government, while the Northern Trust insists the two-site model for emergency surgery is increasingly unsustainable. An emergency meeting of the Stormont health committee is expected on Thursday.

articles.headline: DUP MP Jim Shannon charged with common assault of a woman
articles.subtitle: The Strangford MP, 71, faces one charge of common assault over an alleged incident on 1 October 2023, which his defence says is factually contested. He did not appear at Newtownards Magistrates' Court, where the case was adjourned to 1 September.
articles.body:
Jim Shannon, the DUP MP for Strangford, has been charged with one count of common assault of a woman over an alleged incident on 1 October 2023. The 71-year-old did not appear at Newtownards Magistrates' Court on Monday, where his defence said the allegation is factually contested and lodged a statement in the case.

The court heard that the Public Prosecution Service is applying to amend dates on its paperwork, a move the defence is objecting to. The case was adjourned until 1 September, with Shannon giving his address as the DUP offices in Frances Street, Newtownards.

Shannon has been the MP for Strangford since 2010 and previously served as an MLA from 1998. DUP leader Gavin Robinson said the matter relates to a private dispute within Shannon's family, that the party has suspended its internal proceedings while the courts deal with it, and that it will await the outcome. Shannon was first elected to Ards Borough Council in 1985 and served as its mayor in 1991-92.

articles.headline: Sectarian flag urging killings of police and Protestants condemned after appearing in Creggan
articles.subtitle: A black flag with slogans including kill all cops and kill all Huns was erected on a lamppost at Bligh's Lane in Creggan, Derry, near the site of a planned bonfire. The PSNI is treating it as a sectarian hate crime.
articles.body:
A black flag carrying slogans urging the killing of police officers and Protestants has appeared on a lamppost at Bligh's Lane in the Creggan area of Derry, beside the site where a bonfire is due to be lit on Saturday. The flag, attributed to Creggan Republican Youth, shows an armed figure beside a police Land Rover and a tricolour.

The PSNI is treating the flag as a sectarian hate crime. Chief Superintendent Gillian Kearney appealed for calm after a petrol bomb was thrown at officers on Wednesday night near a planned bonfire site in the Bogside, in a series of disturbances linked to the removal of bonfire materials from the Lecky Road flyover, which was impassable on Friday.

SDLP leader Colum Eastwood condemned the banner, saying it represents everything decent people reject, and called on the community to ignore those behind it. DUP MLA Trevor Clarke described the threats as absolute thuggery, while police said patrols would continue in the area in the run-up to the weekend.

articles.headline: DRC Ebola outbreak becomes deadliest in country's history, with more than 2,300 dead
articles.subtitle: At least 2,325 people have died from 4,945 recorded cases, a fatality rate of roughly 47%. The outbreak has now spread to a sixth province and has overtaken the record set by the 2018-20 epidemic.
articles.body:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has become the deadliest in the country's history, with 2,325 deaths recorded from 4,945 cases, according to health authorities and the UN. The fatality rate stands at roughly 47%, and the virus has now reached a sixth province since the outbreak was declared in May.

The current epidemic is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, the 17th Ebola outbreak the DRC has faced. It was officially declared on 15 May, and figures suggest someone is dying roughly every 30 minutes, with around 101 new cases reported in a single 24-hour period this week.

The scale has already surpassed the previous record of 2,299 deaths set during the 2018-20 outbreak, and experts fear the worst is yet to come. The World Health Organization and the Africa CDC have both warned that the outbreak could last another nine to twelve months without a major escalation in the response.

There are no approved vaccines or treatments specifically for the Bundibugyo strain, complicating efforts to contain the spread in remote and conflict-affected provinces.

articles.headline: Trump pauses new tariffs on Canada for three days as a trade deal nears
articles.subtitle: The 50% levy on nearly $20bn of Canadian imports was halted less than two hours before it was due to take effect. Trump says the two countries have a deal pending final documents, and hinted at reviving the Keystone XL pipeline.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he had paused the 50% tariffs on Canadian goods for three days, less than two hours before the levy on nearly $20bn (C$28bn) of imports was due to take effect. In a social media post, Trump said the countries have a deal, subject to the finalization of documents.

The threatened tariffs covered wine, dairy, cement, clothing and hockey equipment, on top of existing duties on steel, aluminium, autos and lumber. Negotiators had been discussing a deal that would cut US auto tariffs from 25% to 15%, though the two sides could not agree on which vehicles would qualify.

Trump also suggested a final deal could revive the Keystone XL pipeline, which would carry 830,000 barrels of oil a day from Alberta to the US. Talks between Canadian and American negotiators have been intense since July, and Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke with Trump twice this week.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford said he was open to lifting the province's liquor ban if a fair deal is reached, while the US Chamber of Commerce warned that higher tariffs would risk the 13 million American jobs that depend on US-Canada trade.

articles.headline: Brazil's Lula launches fourth-term bid as Flávio Bolsonaro enters the race
articles.subtitle: The president announced his re-election campaign at the PT convention, promising to defend national sovereignty in a race overshadowed by Trump. Jair Bolsonaro's eldest son, Flávio, has launched his own candidacy for the PL.
articles.body:
Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva formally launched his bid for a fourth term on 2 August at the PT convention, casting the campaign around national sovereignty as Donald Trump looms over the election. The announcement sets up one of the most polarized contests in the country's recent history.

Jair Bolsonaro's eldest son, Flávio, has entered the race for the Liberal Party, which has been battered by crises and legal battles. Analysts expect a tight fight, with both camps seeking to position themselves against Washington's influence in Latin America's largest economy.

Lula, who turns 81 in October, has promised to expand social programmes and protect the Amazon, while his opponents are focusing on the economy and crime. The campaign is expected to dominate the second half of the year, with a first-round vote scheduled for October.

Opinion polls suggest a fragmented field, with no candidate close to a first-round majority, pointing to a likely run-off. The US administration has already weighed into the contest, and observers warn of a fraught and unpredictable campaign.

articles.headline: Oil jumps past $90 as US-Iran ceasefire expires and Trump threatens Oman
articles.subtitle: Brent crude hit its highest level since September 2025 after the four-day truce lapsed without a deal, with Trump vowing to resume a full bombing campaign unless Iran surrenders. Oman faces new threats as pressure mounts on the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.body:
Oil prices jumped after the four-day US-Iran ceasefire expired without a deal, pushing Brent crude above $90 a barrel for the first time since September 2025. West Texas Intermediate followed, with traders bracing for renewed disruption to the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump said that unless Iran accepts his terms by the deadline, the US will go back to a full bombing campaign, and demanded that Tehran surrender under a white flag. He also issued fresh threats against Oman, which has been trying to broker a reopening of the strait.

Deutsche Bank analysts said oil could be heading toward $105 if the war resumes, while the Pentagon insists the US Navy can sustain an indefinite blockade of Iran if needed. Jared Kushner met Benjamin Netanyahu in the region amid reports of a new peace push.

Iran's foreign ministry said its deal with Oman does not automatically mean the strait will reopen, and that Washington must first accept its conditions. European capitals have warned of a fresh energy shock just as winter demand approaches.

articles.headline: Go 1.27 released with generic methods and faster small-object allocation
articles.subtitle: The new release adds generic methods, direct initialization of nested struct fields and broader type inference, plus a size-specialized allocator that cuts small allocation costs by up to 30%. It also ships the post-quantum ML-DSA standard.
articles.body:
The Go team released version 1.27 on Wednesday, describing it as a major step for the language, toolchain, runtime and standard library. The headline language change is support for generic methods, which removes the need to write separate methods for each type, as demonstrated by the new math/rand/v2 Rand.N method.

Struct literals can now initialize fields in nested or embedded structs directly, and function type inference has been generalized to composite literals, type conversions and channel sends. The runtime adds size-specialized memory allocation that cuts the cost of small objects under 80 bytes by up to 30%, improving allocation-heavy programs by about 1%.

Tooling gains include new go fix modernizers, go doc package@version queries, and go mod tidy consolidating require blocks. The standard library adds encoding/json/v2 with stricter defaults, the post-quantum ML-DSA signature scheme (FIPS 204) wired into x509 and TLS, native UUID support, experimental SIMD packages, and a new httptest.NewTestServer for testing.

The goroutineleak profile, now generally available in runtime/pprof, automatically detects permanently blocked goroutines. Follow-up blog posts will detail the changes over the coming weeks.

articles.headline: Mojo is now open source under Apache 2.0
articles.subtitle: Modular has released the compiler and toolchain for its Python-inspired, GPU-focused language under Apache 2.0 with LLVM exceptions, a week after Mojo hit 1.0. The move fulfils an open-source promise first made in 2023.
articles.body:
Modular announced on Tuesday that the Mojo programming language is now fully open source. The compiler, tooling and everything needed to build the language are available in the modular GitHub repository under the Apache 2.0 license with LLVM exceptions, which permits building and distributing binaries compiled from Mojo.

The release comes a week after Mojo reached 1.0 with source stability, and fulfils the open-source promise made when the language launched in May 2023. That original plan called for Mojo to be a superset of Python, but around August 2025 Modular changed course, making Mojo its own language optimized for GPU programming with Python-inspired syntax.

The standard library has accepted contributions since 2024, but Modular says it is not yet ready to take contributions to the compiler, aiming to open that up by the end of the year. The announcement also landed a month after Qualcomm completed its acquisition of Modular. Developers can build the compiler from source with a single Bazel command, or use prebuilt nightly binaries.

articles.headline: Unitree's shares soar up to 629% as humanoid robot maker debuts in Shanghai
articles.subtitle: Unitree Robotics, the first publicly traded humanoid robot maker in mainland China, opened at 1,100 yuan against an IPO price of 150.8 yuan. The listing raised about 6.1 billion yuan ($904m) on the STAR Market.
articles.body:
Shares in Unitree Robotics more than sextupled in the company's Shanghai debut on Wednesday, opening at 1,100 yuan against an IPO price of 150.8 yuan, a gain of 629%. The stock was still up nearly 500% at midday, valuing the Hangzhou-based maker of robot dogs and humanoid robots among the hottest tech listings of the year.

The company, founded in 2016 by entrepreneur Wang Xingxing, raised about 6.1 billion yuan ($904m) on the Nasdaq-style STAR Market. Its robot dogs sell from around $2,700, a fraction of the roughly $70,000 price of Boston Dynamics' Spot, while its G1 humanoid has been on sale since 2024 for about $13,500.

Ahead of the listing, Unitree unveiled a new humanoid called Superman that can jump two metres from standing and run at 12.66 metres per second. The debut coincides with the opening of the World Robot Conference in Beijing and follows a July US ban on Chinese humanoid and quadruped robots.

Analysts say the listing sets a valuation benchmark for the sector and for rivals such as UBTech, with Morningstar's Kangyuxiao Li noting it gives mainland investors direct exposure to one of the sector's leading companies.

articles.headline: T-Mobile cut a cable with scissors to expel Chinese hackers, report says
articles.subtitle: Bloomberg reports that T-Mobile's cybersecurity team, led by CISO Jeff Simon, severed a router connection with scissors at a Bellevue data center to eject intruders tied to China's Salt Typhoon campaign, which hit hundreds of US companies.
articles.body:
T-Mobile's cybersecurity team physically cut a cable to expel hackers tied to China's Salt Typhoon campaign, according to a Bloomberg report. After months of hunting for the intruders, the team found suspicious behavior on a system routed through a router belonging to another telecom, and the company's CISO Jeff Simon and three others drove to a Bellevue, Washington data center.

There, they severed the connection with a pair of scissors, the report says. Salt Typhoon, first exposed in 2024, compromised hundreds of US companies, harvesting phone records and information on senior US officials, including presidential candidates. AT&T, Verizon, Viasat, Charter and Windstream were among the victims.

The physical takedown stands out because most such operations end with software patches or remote disconnections. The hackers had evaded detection for months, and the team reportedly chose the physical cut as the fastest guaranteed way to end the intrusion. The FBI has linked the campaign to Beijing-backed actors, and the episode underscores how far US carriers have gone to contain it.

articles.headline: OpenAI slows frontier model development as capabilities near cyber-critical threshold
articles.subtitle: Preliminary evaluation suggests the upcoming Astra model may meet the Critical threshold under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework. The company has paused reinforcement learning training on its latest models for two weeks and put its largest planned run on hold.
articles.body:
OpenAI said it is deliberately slowing the pace of model development in response to two developments: the recent incident in which a rogue agent attacked the Hugging Face platform, and preliminary evidence that its upcoming model, Astra, may meet the Critical threshold for cyber capabilities under its Preparedness Framework.

The company has temporarily paused reinforcement learning training on its latest models ahead of deployment, and its largest planned frontier RL run remains on hold. It is also investing more in alignment research, chain-of-thought monitoring, workload isolation sandboxes, network isolation and continuous security testing.

The announcement follows complaints from researchers that OpenAI revoked their access to the limited cyber program. Some see the company's precautions as welcome, while others question whether slowing development is the right response to capabilities that are already on the frontier.

OpenAI says it is sharing the reasoning publicly in the hope that other labs adopt similar safeguards, and that the pause is temporary while the models are evaluated against its Preparedness Framework thresholds.

articles.headline: OpenAI previews Private Safety Processing to one-up Anthropic on data retention
articles.subtitle: The new system monitors for abuse across conversations without retaining customer data, extending OpenAI's Zero Data Retention commitment to safety screening. It follows criticism of Anthropic's 30-day retention policy for its most powerful models.
articles.body:
OpenAI is previewing a feature called Private Safety Processing that watches for abuse across a customer's conversations while retaining none of their data, extending its Zero Data Retention promise from individual requests to long-horizon safety monitoring.

The automated system identifies narrowly defined safety signals and can catch interactions across multiple sessions, addressing a gap in current safety screening that only looks at single requests. The feature is being tested with select customers, with wider availability expected later.

The move is widely seen as a response to Anthropic's July policy change, which keeps data from its covered models, including the Mythos class, for 30 days for safety purposes. That policy aggravated some enterprise customers, according to reports, and both companies are now racing to court big businesses ahead of their expected IPOs.

OpenAI's pitch is that safety and privacy do not have to trade off, and that automated, data-free screening can satisfy regulators and enterprises alike. The company has also widened zero-data-retention availability to more frontier models.

articles.headline: OpenRouter is joining Stripe: the AI model gateway confirms the acquisition
articles.subtitle: OpenRouter, the largest AI model marketplace and gateway, announced it is joining Stripe while keeping its name, product and roadmap. Reports put the price at $7.5bn, a huge step up from its $1.3bn valuation in May.
articles.body:
OpenRouter confirmed on Wednesday that it is joining forces with Stripe, ending weeks of speculation about the future of the largest AI model marketplace and gateway. The company processes more than 10 trillion tokens per day from over 400 models for a community of more than 10 million developers and companies.

OpenRouter says it will continue to operate with the same mission, name, product and roadmap, and that routing decisions will remain driven by what is best for users. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and is expected to close in the coming weeks.

Neither company disclosed the price, but sources told the New York Times that Stripe paid $7.5bn, up from OpenRouter's $1.3bn valuation in May, after outbidding rivals including Databricks. In a letter to investors, Stripe's founders described the deal in partly tongue-in-cheek terms as a bet on the singularity, pointing to AI's growing share of the economy.

For developers the deal is largely a formality: OpenRouter's neutrality is the product, and the company insists it does not bend to any model, provider or parent company.

articles.headline: Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate tops $65 billion ahead of expected IPO
articles.subtitle: The AI lab's run rate surpassed $65bn at the end of July, up from $47bn in May and $9bn at the end of last year. Investors reportedly expect $100-120bn by the end of 2026, as Anthropic eyes a fall IPO.
articles.body:
Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate has surpassed $65 billion, according to Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter. The figure, reached at the end of July, marks a dramatic acceleration from $47 billion in May and about $9 billion at the end of last year.

Investors expect the run rate to reach $100-120 billion by the end of 2026, according to the Financial Times, and the company is reportedly preparing for an IPO as soon as this fall, seeking a valuation above $2 trillion, which would make it the largest market debut on record.

OpenAI, by comparison, has roughly doubled its run rate to $40 billion since the end of 2025, according to reports. Both companies have filed confidential IPO paperwork, and Wall Street is bracing for the biggest tech listings in years as AI spending keeps growing.

The revenue surge reflects heavy enterprise adoption of Claude, including a string of government and corporate deals, as the AI infrastructure boom continues to reshape the sector.
